name: Trucker Path
subcategory: trucking navigation and truck stop data
tagline: Truck-legal GPS routing plus crowdsourced truck stop, parking and weigh station info for commercial drivers.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely build a map with pins on it in an afternoon. What you cannot build is a live feed of which truck stops have parking open at 9pm on a Tuesday, contributed by hundreds of thousands of drivers who are already there. The routing side is worse: truck-legal directions need bridge clearances, weight limits, hazmat restrictions and state-by-state truck route designations, and getting that wrong is not a bug, it is a decapitated trailer. Open data covers some of it unevenly and nobody sane bets a CDL on a hobby build. Build the trip notebook, keep paying for the routing.
coreLoopDIY: A personal offline map of truck stops and rest areas you have actually used, with your own notes on parking, showers, overnight tolerance and gate hours, plus a simple multi-stop trip list.
requirements: OpenStreetMap tiles or a self-hosted tile source
OSM Overpass extract for amenity=truck_stop, highway=rest_area, amenity=fuel
a phone browser you are willing to install a PWA on
offline storage, because coverage on I-80 in Nevada is a rumor
whatYouLose: Live crowdsourced parking availability, which is the entire reason people open the app at dusk
Truck-legal routing with bridge heights, weight limits and hazmat restrictions
Weigh station open/closed reports and scale bypass context
Fuel prices, discount network pricing and IFTA-friendly fuel stop planning
A maintained POI database that reflects stops closing, gates changing and lots getting paved over
moatNotes: The parking data has a hard liquidity floor: it only works because enough drivers report from the same lots on the same night. A directory with three users reports nothing.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is circling an industrial park at 10pm with 20 minutes left on your clock. Drivers pay for the crowd, not the software: real time parking reports, current stop details, and routing that will not send an 80,000 pound vehicle under a 12 foot 6 bridge. Every one of those depends on either a large active user base or a licensed commercial road attribute dataset, and a personal build has neither. The map UI is the cheap part and always was.
notes: The map is a weekend; the lot at midnight is not. The moat is a live crowd of drivers reporting parking plus licensed truck-legal road attributes, and neither one exists for an audience of one.
prompt:
Build a local-first PWA called "RigNotes": a personal truck stop notebook and trip list for one driver. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- MapLibre GL JS for the map
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for all storage
- vite-plugin-pwa for offline install and asset caching
- Tailwind for styling, dark by default, big tap targets for use in a cab

Data bootstrap:
- Include a script scripts/fetch-pois.ts that queries the OSM Overpass API for amenity=truck_stop, highway=rest_area, amenity=fuel with hgv=yes inside a bounding box passed as CLI args, and writes public/pois.geojson.
- Do NOT ship a prebuilt dataset. Document in README that this is OSM data, may be stale or wrong, and is not truck-legal routing.
- Read OVERPASS_URL from .env with a sensible default. Never hardcode secrets.

Features, in scope:
1. Map view with POI pins, cluster at low zoom, tap a pin to open a sheet.
2. Per-POI personal record: star rating, parking notes, spaces guess, shower yes/no, overnight tolerated yes/no/unknown, gate hours text, free-form notes, last visited date. All stored locally.
3. "I parked here" button that stamps a visit with timestamp and optional note.
4. Trip list: ordered list of saved stops with drag reorder, per-leg mileage typed by hand, plus running total. No routing engine.
5. Search and filter by name, my rating, shower, overnight-ok, visited-in-last-N-days.
6. Export and import all personal data as JSON. This is the backup story.
7. Offline: cached tiles for a user-selected region via a simple "download this area" button, plus full function with no network.

Out of scope, do not build:
- Routing, bridge heights, weight limits, hazmat restrictions
- Live parking availability, fuel prices, weigh station status
- Any multi-user or sync feature

Ship a README with setup, the Overpass fetch command, and a blunt safety note that this tool does not provide truck-legal directions.
